title: Project Overview
description: README.md describes what lodestone is: a fully offline desktop app that helps musicians practice, with a tuner, auto-generated play-along charts, and a scoring mode. Reading it first sets the context for every architectural decision you will encounter — why there is a heavy ML pipeline, why the UI must never import torch, and why the app must run on battery with no internet connection.

title: Architecture Contract
description: ARCHITECTURE.md is the authoritative reference for the module graph, the exact JSON shapes passed between modules (handoff contracts), and the five chart guarantees the app must satisfy. Every module in the codebase is designed to conform to these shapes; understanding them before reading any source file will make the data flowing between modules immediately recognizable.

title: Project Configuration
description: pyproject.toml defines the project's build metadata, pins Python to 3.12, and lists dependencies. The ML stack (Demucs, Basic Pitch) is grouped under an optional 'ml' extra so a developer can install just the UI dependencies without pulling in the heavyweight models. This split mirrors the architectural boundary between the UI process and the background prep process.
languageLesson: In Python projects managed with uv or pip, optional dependency groups (extras_require / [project.optional-dependencies]) let you declare heavyweight dependencies separately from core ones. Installing 'package[ml]' vs 'package' gives you different dependency sets from the same pyproject.toml.

title: Central Storage Layer
description: store.py is the single most depended-upon module in the codebase, with a fan-in of 7 — every pipeline step and the GUI all go through it. It owns the song folder layout and enforces atomic JSON writes (write to a temp file, then rename) so a crash mid-write can never corrupt a song record. Understanding this module's API is the prerequisite for understanding every other module.
languageLesson: Atomic file writes in Python use the write-then-rename pattern: write data to a sibling temp file, then call os.replace() (or pathlib Path.rename()). On POSIX this is a single atomic syscall; on Windows, os.replace() handles the swap. This guarantees readers never see a partially written file.

title: Pitch Detection Algorithm
description: pitch.py implements the YIN algorithm, which estimates the fundamental frequency of a monophonic audio frame by finding the lag at which a signal best repeats itself. It operates purely on a NumPy array and returns a PitchReading with frequency and confidence values. This is the low-level primitive that powers the real-time tuner.
languageLesson: YIN is a time-domain pitch detection algorithm. It computes a difference function over a window of audio samples, normalizes it, and finds the first minimum below a confidence threshold. Because it works in the time domain it is computationally lightweight — suitable for real-time use on battery without a GPU.

title: Tuner Smoothing and Display
description: tuner.py wraps the raw PitchReading values from pitch.py with a smoothing pass to suppress jitter between frames, then converts the stabilized frequency into a TunerDisplay: the nearest note name, cents deviation, and an in-tune flag. The separation between raw detection (pitch.py) and display logic (tuner.py) keeps each function focused and independently testable.

title: Desktop GUI
description: dev_gui.py is the application shell. It hosts three tabs — TunerTab, SongsTab, and ChartTab — and wires together the modules introduced so far: it drives the audio loop through pitch.py and tuner.py, calls ingest.py when a user drops in a song, and delegates prep work to jobs.py. Its high fan-out (5 direct imports) reflects its role as the composition root; it is a coordinator, not a logic container.
languageLesson: Tkinter organizes a window with geometry managers (pack, grid, place) and a main event loop (mainloop()). Long-running work — like audio capture or ML processing — must run in a separate thread or process, because blocking the event loop freezes the whole UI. Lodestone uses multiprocessing for the prep pipeline precisely to keep the GUI responsive.

title: Song Ingest
description: ingest.py handles the first step a user takes: adding a song to the library. It computes a SHA-256 hash of the audio file to use as a stable, content-based ID, copies the file into the song folder, and writes the initial song.json via store.py. Using a content hash as the ID means importing the same file twice is idempotent and deduplicated automatically.

title: Stem Separation
description: separate.py runs Demucs (the htdemucs_6s model) on the ingested audio to split the song into six stems: vocals, bass, drums, guitar, piano, and other. It then mixes all non-guitar stems into a single backing-track WAV so the user can practice guitar against the full band minus themselves. All paths are resolved and written through store.py.
languageLesson: Demucs is a waveform-domain source separation model. The '6s' variant separates into six stems using a U-Net architecture trained on mixture-to-stem pairs. Running it on CPU on a laptop takes roughly 2-5x real-time, so it must run in a background process, not the UI thread.

title: Pitch Transcription
description: transcribe.py runs Basic Pitch on the guitar stem WAV produced by separate.py. Unlike the monophonic YIN detector used for real-time tuning, Basic Pitch is a polyphonic model that returns a list of note events, each with onset time, offset time, pitch, and velocity. These raw events are the input to the chart builder in the next step.

title: Chart Building
description: chart.py takes the raw note events from transcribe.py and applies a multi-step cleaning pipeline — deduplication, octave shifting to keep notes in guitar range, and string/fret assignment — to produce a playable guitar chart. The five guarantees from ARCHITECTURE.md (notes in range, valid fret numbers, no overlapping notes on the same string, etc.) are all enforced here.

title: Background Job Orchestration
description: jobs.py is the boundary between the UI process and the ML pipeline. It launches the full prep sequence (ingest, separate, transcribe, chart) inside a separate multiprocessing.Process so the Tkinter event loop is never blocked by the heavy model inference. This module is also the enforcement point for the architectural rule that the UI never imports torch or Basic Pitch.

title: Test Suite and Fixtures
description: The test suite is organized around the same layers as the source: test_pitch_tuner.py verifies the YIN detector and tuner against synthesized sine waves; test_chart_guarantees.py enforces each of the five chart guarantees in isolation; test_store.py covers atomic writes and schema validation; test_formats.py validates fixture JSON files against the handoff shapes from ARCHITECTURE.md; and test_prep.py runs the full pipeline end-to-end. conftest.py generates a sample WAV on first run so all tests can operate offline.
languageLesson: Pytest's conftest.py is auto-loaded before any test in the same directory tree. Fixtures defined there (with @pytest.fixture) are available to all tests without an explicit import. Session-scoped fixtures (scope='session') run once per test run, making them ideal for expensive setup like synthesizing an audio file.
